mainTopic: Conditions waiving אונאה, the laws of selling באמנה (on trust), and the start of the משנה on worn coins.
overview: The גמרא finishes a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל about selling on condition that there will be no claim of אונאה. רב says the condition fails, because the other side never knowingly gave up anything. שמואל says it works, because it is not certain that any Torah law is being uprooted. רב ענן reports that שמואל drew a line between 'you have no claim against me,' which works, and 'there is no אונאה in it,' which fails. A ברייתא that lets the condition work challenges רב. אביי answers that רב follows רבי מאיר and שמואל follows רבי יהודה. רבא answers instead that רב means an ordinary case and the ברייתא means a case where the real value was stated openly, and a second ברייתא supports him. Next the גמרא brings the laws of someone who sells באמנה, on trust: he must price all his goods the same way, and he may charge for his expenses but not for his own work. Finally a new משנה begins, asking how worn a סלע can be before spending it at full value counts as אונאה. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב's reasoning: the other side never knowingly gave up his rights
steps.stepSummary: רב finishes explaining why even רבי יהודה would agree that the condition does not work in a case of אונאה. The other party does not know he is being overcharged, so he cannot truly give up his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, does he know that there is something to give up?
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב's explanation from just before. רבי יהודה lets people make monetary conditions only when the other side knowingly gives up his rights, and in a sale nobody knows an overcharge is coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's rule is based on knowingly giving something up (מחילה). When someone agrees to 'no אונאה claim,' he thinks the price is fair and does not know he is losing anything. So his agreement is not a real, informed waiver, and the Torah's protection stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: here (in our case of a sale)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying that רבי יהודה changes his opinion. רבי יהודה still allows monetary conditions. רב is pointing out that the reason behind his rule, a knowing waiver, is missing in a case of אונאה.

phrases.english: But here,
does he know, so that he could give it up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב's statement 'I hold this even according to רבי יהודה' from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of אונאה, a condition giving up the claim does not work, because the victim does not knowingly waive anything.

steps.title: שמואל holds the condition works, even according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that even רבי מאיר, who is strict about conditions against the Torah, would let this condition work. רבי מאיר is strict only when the Torah law is definitely being uprooted, and here maybe no overcharge will happen at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: I hold my view even according to רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר only said his ruling there, where the person definitely uproots a Torah law. But here, who says he is uprooting anything?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the reasoning for his side: the condition works, and he says even רבי מאיר would agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר cancels conditions that go against the Torah, but only where the Torah law is definitely being uprooted. In a sale, there may be no overcharge at all, so the condition might never actually cancel any Torah law. Because the uprooting is not certain, רבי מאיר's strict rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: he only said his ruling (in that specific case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two sides are really arguing about the nature of the condition. רב focuses on whether the waiver is a knowing one, and שמואל focuses on whether a Torah law is certainly being uprooted.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
I said my view even according to Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir only said his ruling there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means רבי מאיר's case of קידושין with a condition, which the גמרא discussed just before.

phrases.english: where he definitely uproots a Torah law,
but here, who says
that he is uprooting anything?
phrases.notes: Maybe the price will turn out fair, and then the condition never cancels anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: אֲנָא דַּאֲמַרִי אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side's reasoning, matching רב's 'even according to רבי יהודה' with 'even according to רבי מאיר.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition giving up the claim of אונאה works, because it is not certain that any Torah law is being uprooted.

steps.title: רב ענן reports how שמואל explained his view: the wording decides
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן says שמואל told him personally that it depends on the wording. 'You will have no אונאה claim against me' works. 'There is no אונאה in this sale' does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: מר שמואל explained this to me himself. If someone says to his friend, 'on condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me,' he has no claim of אונאה against him. If he says, 'on condition that there is no אונאה in it,' then there is אונאה in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן adds an important detail about שמואל's view: it matters exactly how the condition is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'You have no claim against me' is a personal waiver of money, which a person may give up. 'There is no אונאה in this sale' tries to say the Torah law itself does not apply here, which is a direct attempt to cancel the Torah. So שמואל's leniency covers only the first wording.

keyTerms.meaning: overcharging or underpaying beyond the allowed amount

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל: 'no claim against ME' means the condition works and there is no אונאה. 'No אונאה IN IT' means the condition fails and the law of אונאה applies.
steps.confusionAlert: The two wordings sound almost the same, but they give opposite results. The first gives up a personal claim. The second tries to cancel the Torah's law itself.

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
To me personally it was explained
by Mar Shmuel:
One who says to his fellow,
'on condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me' —
he has no claim of אונאה against him.
'On condition that there is no אונאה in it' —
then there is אונאה in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עָנָן: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows שמואל's view from Step 2 so it covers only one wording of the condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition worded as a personal waiver ('no claim against me') works. A condition worded as canceling the law ('no אונאה in it') does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the condition works — who taught it, according to רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says 'no claim of אונאה against me' works. Since רב said that even רבי יהודה would hold the condition fails, it seems no תנא is left who could have taught this ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who does business on trust, and one who says to his friend 'on condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me,' has no claim of אונאה against him. According to רב, who said 'I hold my view even according to רבי יהודה,' whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that clearly lets the condition work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is the stricter תנא about conditions, and רב claimed that even the more lenient רבי יהודה would agree that the condition fails in a case of אונאה. If neither תנא would allow it, the ברייתא saying the condition works has no author. This is a strong problem for רב, and it matches שמואל's view exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: one who does business on trust

phrases.english: They challenged:
One who does business on trust,
phrases.notes: This is a deal where one side relies on the other's word about the price, so it is a separate case from the condition that follows.

phrases.english: and one who says to his fellow,
'on condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me' —
he has no claim of אונאה against him.
According to Rav, who said:
'I said my view even according to Rabbi Yehuda,'
whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רב's view from Step 1 and attacks it with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that even רבי יהודה would say the condition of 'no אונאה claim' fails.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה would say the condition fails, no תנא is left to author a ברייתא that says it works.

steps.title: אביי says רב follows רבי מאיר and שמואל follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers the challenge by changing who רב and שמואל follow: רב goes with רבי מאיר, and שמואל goes with רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is clear that רב holds like רבי מאיר, and שמואל holds like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from step 4. He says רב was not really explaining רבי יהודה. רב follows רבי מאיר, and the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, just like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that no תנא seemed to fit the ברייתא. אביי fixes this by saying רב's view that the condition fails comes from רבי מאיר. That leaves רבי יהודה free to be the תנא of the ברייתא, where the condition works, and this matches שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of רבי מאיר
According to the view of רבי יהודה

steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, רב said that 'even רבי יהודה' would agree the condition fails. אביי drops that idea and gives רב's view to רבי מאיר alone.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is clear,
Rav spoke according to Rabbi Meir,
and Shmuel, who spoke, spoke according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: So the ברייתא from step 4, where the condition works, follows רבי יהודה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning which תנא each אמורא follows
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said even רבי יהודה holds the condition fails, so no תנא is left for the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי מאיר, and the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, as שמואל does

steps.title: רבא separates an ordinary case from a case where the price gap is stated openly
steps.stepSummary: רבא keeps רב's explanation of רבי יהודה. He says רב spoke about an ordinary case, and the ברייתא speaks about a case where the overcharge is spelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: There is no difficulty. One ruling is about an ordinary case, and the other is about a case where it was spelled out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the challenge. He says there is no contradiction, because the two rulings deal with two different kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an ordinary case (סתם), the other side does not know how big the overcharge is. So רבי יהודה agrees the condition fails, just as רב said. In the ברייתא, the price gap is stated openly (מפרש), so the other side knowingly gives up his claim, and the condition works.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
An ordinary case, with no details spelled out
Spelling it out; stating the details openly

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to רב's reason in step 1: a person can only give up an אונאה claim if he knows about the overcharge.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult;
here, it is an ordinary case;
phrases.notes: This 'here' is רב's case, where the condition fails.

phrases.english: here, it is where he spells it out.
phrases.notes: This 'here' is the ברייתא's case, where the condition works.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from אביי to the same challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא contradict each other about רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means an ordinary case and the ברייתא means an open case, so both fit רבי יהודה

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the difference between an ordinary case and an open case
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the earlier rule applies only in an ordinary case. When the seller or buyer states the real value openly, the condition works.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: When does this apply? In an ordinary case. But when it is spelled out, the condition works. For example, a seller tells the buyer: 'I am selling you this item for two hundred, and I know it is worth only one hundred, on condition that you have no אונאה claim against me.' Then the buyer has no claim. The same applies to a buyer who tells the seller: 'I am buying it for one hundred, and I know it is worth two hundred, on condition that you have no אונאה claim against me.' Then the seller has no claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רבא's split between an ordinary case and an open case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא openly uses the same two words רבא used: סתם and מפרש. It gives two examples, an overcharging seller and an underpaying buyer. In both, the real value is stated, so the waiver is made knowingly and it works.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth one hundred זוז
Overcharging or underpaying in a sale

steps.whatToRemember: An אונאה waiver works only when the other side knows the real value. In an ordinary case it fails. When the gap is stated openly, it works.

phrases.english: As it is taught: When is this said? In an ordinary case.
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule that the condition does not work.

phrases.english: But where he spells it out,
for example, a seller who said to the buyer:

phrases.aramaic: חֵפֶץ זֶה שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ בְּמָאתַיִם
phrases.english: This item that I am selling you for two hundred,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי בּוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה אֶלָּא מָנֶה.
phrases.english: I know that it is worth only one hundred.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְךָ עָלַי אוֹנָאָה –
phrases.english: I sell it on condition that you have no overcharge claim against me,
then he has no overcharge claim against him.
And likewise, a buyer who said to the seller:

phrases.aramaic: חֵפֶץ זֶה שֶׁאֲנִי לוֹקֵחַ מִמְּךָ בְּמָנֶה
phrases.english: This item that I am buying from you for one hundred,
I know that it is worth two hundred.

phrases.aramaic: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֵין לְךָ עָלַי אוֹנָאָה –
phrases.english: I buy it on condition that you have no overcharge claim against me,
then he has no overcharge claim against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that backs up רבא's answer
steps.raayaObject: רבא's split between סתם and מפרש
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses the words סתם and מפרש and gives the seller and buyer examples

steps.title: Someone doing business on trust must price everything the same way
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that a person who sells באמנה cannot price the poor goods on trust and the good goods at market value. He must use one method for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person who does business on trust may not price the poor-quality goods on trust and the good-quality goods at market value. He must price both on trust, or both at market value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ברייתא about a related business topic: selling באמנה, on trust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A seller could mix the two methods so that he always gets the better price, which would cheat the buyer. The ברייתא blocks this by requiring one consistent method for all the goods.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who does business on trust,
phrases.notes: 'On trust' means the buyer relies on the seller to say what he paid, and then adds an agreed profit.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יְחַשֵּׁב אֶת הָרַע בַּאֲמָנָה
phrases.english: may not price the poor-quality goods on trust
and the good-quality goods at market value.
Rather, he must price either both on trust,
or both at market value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic. It is brought because the ברייתא in step 4 mentioned הנושא ונותן באמנה, and now the גמרא cites a ברייתא that gives the laws of that arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who sells באמנה must price all the goods by one method, either all on trust or all at market value

steps.title: The seller may charge his expenses but not his own wages
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a seller who sells באמנה may charge the buyer for porters, camel drivers and lodging, but not for his own work, because he was already paid in full.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the buyer pays him for the porter, for the camel driver, and for the inn. But the seller does not take a fee for his own work, because he was already given his full wages.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step keeps going. It now lists which costs the seller may add when he sells באמנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When selling באמנה, the buyer relies on the seller's word about what the goods cost him. Real money the seller spent, like porters, camels and inns, he may pass on. He may not add a fee for his own effort, because he was already paid for that from another source, as steps 10-11 explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Porter, someone hired to carry loads
His own wages, payment for his own time and effort

phrases.english: And he gives him the porter's fee,
phrases.notes: The buyer pays the seller back for what the seller spent hiring a porter.

phrases.english: the camel driver's fee, the inn fee.
His own wages, he does not take,
since he was already given his wages in full.
phrases.notes: The one who gave him his wages is the supplier he bought the goods from, not the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא about selling באמנה that began in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller באמנה may recover his real expenses (porter, camel, lodging) but may not charge for his own labor, since he was already paid in full.

steps.title: Where did the seller get his full wages from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who paid the seller his full wages, as the ברייתא claims.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wages in full: from where were they given to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's last line. It wants to know who paid the seller for his work. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the seller already got his full wages. But it does not say who paid him or how. The גמרא wants to see the actual source of that payment.

phrases.english: His wages in full,
from where does he give it to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׂכָרוֹ מִשָּׁלֵם מֵהֵיכָא קָא יָהֵיב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of the ברייתא's claim in step 9 that the seller was already paid in full.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who pays the seller his full wages, and in what form?

steps.title: רב פפא: the supplier adds four per hundred
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is talking about sellers of cheap garments, whose suppliers give four extra units for every hundred bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is about sellers of cheap garments, where the supplier gives four extra for every hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. He says the seller's wages come from the supplier, who adds a few free units to every large order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cheap-garment trade, the supplier gives four extra items for every hundred the seller buys. Those extra items are the seller's payment for his effort. So if he also charged the buyer for his work, he would be paid twice.
steps.whatToRemember: Selling באמנה: the seller passes on his real expenses but not a fee for his own work, because the supplier's bonus of four per hundred already pays him.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With sellers of cheap garments,
where they give four for a hundred.
phrases.notes: The supplier throws in four extra units for every hundred bought, and that bonus is the seller's pay.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seller's wages come from the supplier, who gives four extra units for every hundred purchased.

steps.title: New משנה: how worn can a סלע be?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה asks how much a סלע coin can be worn down and still be spent at full value without אונאה. רבי מאיר says four איסרות (one per דינר), רבי יהודה says four פונדיונות (one per דינר), and רבי שמעון begins to give his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How much can a סלע be worn down and still not count as אונאה? רבי מאיר says: four איסרות, one איסר per דינר. רבי יהודה says: four פונדיונות, one פונדיון per דינר. And רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from overcharging on goods to coins that have lost value from wear, and asks how much loss is still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is worth four דינרים. רבי מאיר allows a loss of one איסר per דינר, which is 1/24 of the coin. רבי יהודה allows twice that, one פונדיון per דינר, which is 1/12 of the coin. רבי שמעון's amount continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin worth four דינרים
Lacking, worn down below full weight
A small coin, 1/24 of a דינר
A coin worth two איסרים, 1/12 of a דינר
A silver coin; four make a סלע

steps.confusionAlert: The amounts are given for the whole סלע: four איסרות in total, which works out to one per דינר. They are not four per דינר.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How much may the sela be lacking
and still there will be no overcharging with it?
Rabbi Meir says: four issars,
an issar per dinar.
And Rabbi Yehuda says: four pundeyons,
a pundeyon per dinar.
And Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה תְּהֵא הַסֶּלַע חֲסֵירָה וְלֹא יְהֵא בָּהּ אוֹנָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה, moving from overcharging on goods to the law of worn coins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A worn סלע may be spent at full value without אונאה up to a set loss: רבי מאיר says four איסרות (one per דינר), and רבי יהודה says four פונדיונות (one per דינר). רבי שמעון's view follows.
